description: The six description archetypes of the source catalog. catalog_template rebuilds any capability's description from its subject; sections is the section contract a spec must satisfy for that archetype; gates and evidence_kinds are what closes the work; inference_rules classify a capability named in a user's own file.
usage_order: match the stored description against catalog_template
if it matches, the archetype and subject are authoritative
if it does not, apply inference_rules to the capability name and generate the catalog wording from catalog_template
render sections in order; a section is only satisfied when every field is filled or explicitly marked unknown

implement.label: Implement
implement.intent: Build one reusable production capability end to end, with declared boundaries, offline inputs, measured budgets, and acceptance proof.

gates.rule: every consumed and produced asset has a license record that permits this project's use and redistribution
each named metric is measured on the declared target and inside its ceiling
a clean machine reproduces the build from the offline bundle with no hidden download
the capability passes on a real target build, not only in the editor

sections.title: Declared inputs
sections.purpose: Every file, setting, and local dependency the capability consumes, with the pinned offline location.

sections.title: Declared outputs
sections.purpose: Artifacts produced, their format contract, destination, and the consumer of each one.

sections.title: Offline dependencies
sections.purpose: Cached engine modules, packages, models, and toolchains required with the network blocked.

sections.title: Rights metadata
sections.purpose: License and provenance record for each consumed and produced asset.

sections.title: Performance budgets
sections.purpose: Numeric ceilings the capability must stay inside on the declared target profile.

sections.title: Diagnostics
sections.purpose: Structured signals that show what the capability did and why it failed.

sections.title: Tests
sections.purpose: Automated checks that must run in the local test path before the capability is called done.

sections.title: Target-build acceptance criteria
sections.purpose: Observable acceptance on a real target build, not only in the editor.

implement.catalog_template: Implement {subject} as a focused reusable game-development capability with declared inputs and outputs, offline dependencies, rights metadata, performance budgets, diagnostics, tests, and target-build acceptance criteria.

define.label: Define
define.intent: Settle a decision and its boundaries in writing, with named owners and constraints, so downstream work has one reference to build against.

gates.rule: the boundary and the non-goals are written down and accepted by the named owners
every decision in scope has one accountable role
platform, engine, and rights constraints were verified against the offline bundle, not assumed
the completion condition was tested against a real case

sections.title: Prerequisites
sections.purpose: What must exist or be decided before this definition can be written down at all.

sections.title: Owners and decision rights
sections.purpose: Who defines, who reviews, and who can change the definition later.

sections.title: Platform and engine constraints
sections.purpose: Hard limits from the engine, the platform, and the offline environment.

sections.title: Ordered steps
sections.purpose: The sequence the definition prescribes, each with its output.

sections.title: License gates
sections.purpose: Rights conditions that stop this definition from shipping as written.

sections.title: Quality budgets
sections.purpose: The numeric or observable bar the result must clear, with how it is measured.

sections.title: Fallback paths
sections.purpose: What the team does when the preferred route is unavailable offline.

sections.title: Required evidence
sections.purpose: The artefacts that prove the definition was followed.

sections.title: Verified completion condition
sections.purpose: The one sentence that says this is done, and how it was tested.

define.catalog_template: Define {subject} with prerequisites, owners, platform and engine constraints, ordered steps, license gates, quality budgets, fallback paths, required evidence, and a verified completion condition.

evaluate.label: Evaluate
evaluate.intent: Measure a real build or asset against a stated threshold with repeatable checks, and record the evidence, the failure detail, and the retest.

gates.rule: each check names its tool, its threshold, and its fixture before it runs
every automated and manual check has a recorded result on the declared target
measured values are stored beside the threshold they were judged against
a failed check has remediation and a passing retest attached

sections.title: Check design
sections.purpose: What is checked, how, and how often, decided before any measurement.

sections.title: Automated checks
sections.purpose: Checks that run in the local test path with a pass threshold.

sections.title: Manual checks
sections.purpose: Checks that need a human on a device, with the protocol written down.

sections.title: Measured results
sections.purpose: The numbers actually observed, with unit and profile.

sections.title: Failure evidence
sections.purpose: What a failure leaves behind that someone else can read.

sections.title: Remediation
sections.purpose: The fix owed for each failure, with its owner.

sections.title: Regression retest
sections.purpose: How the fix is proven and where the retest is filed.

evaluate.catalog_template: Evaluate {subject} with repeatable automated and manual checks, record the engine, platform, hardware, scene or build, measured result, pass threshold, failure evidence, and exact remediation and regression retest.

operate.label: Operate
operate.intent: Run a service or toolchain day to day with monitoring, budgets, an owner on call, and a rehearsed rollback.

gates.rule: the runbook was followed start to finish by someone who did not write it
each signal has a threshold and an alert route that fired in a drill
the revert path was executed and measured on a real build
the owning team accepted the operating responsibility in writing

sections.title: Runbook
sections.purpose: The steps to start, observe, and stop the thing, with expected output.

sections.title: Monitoring
sections.purpose: Signals watched continuously, with thresholds and routes.

sections.title: Incident response
sections.purpose: What to do first when it breaks, and who is told.

sections.title: Maintenance and rollback
sections.purpose: Scheduled work and the tested way back.

sections.title: Health budgets
sections.purpose: Operating limits that, once crossed, mean the service is unhealthy.

operate.catalog_template: Operate {subject} through versioned configuration, bounded CPU, GPU, memory, storage, and network budgets, safe persistence, structured diagnostics, offline fallback behavior, and automated gameplay regression tests.

create.label: Create
create.intent: Produce a build or generated artifact from pinned inputs, reproducibly, and prove it works after creation.

gates.rule: every input has a version and a checksum recorded with the offline bundle
each input and each produced asset cleared its license gate
two runs from the same pinned inputs produce the same artifact set
the produced artifact imports, launches, or plays on the target

sections.title: Pinned local inputs
sections.purpose: Exact input set, version, and local location; no hidden downloads.

sections.title: License and integrity checks
sections.purpose: Rights verification and checksum verification before the build starts.

sections.title: Deterministic settings
sections.purpose: Settings frozen so two runs produce the same result.

sections.title: Platform metadata
sections.purpose: Manifest fields, version strings, and platform identifiers carried by the artifact.

sections.title: Rollback or cleanup
sections.purpose: How a bad output is reverted or removed without leaving state behind.

sections.title: Post-build validation
sections.purpose: Import, launch, or playback proof that the produced artifact actually works.

create.catalog_template: Create {subject} from pinned local inputs with license and integrity checks, deterministic settings, platform metadata, rollback or cleanup behavior, and a post-build import, launch, or playback validation.

provide.label: Provide
provide.intent: Ship a reusable interface, kit, or template to other teams with a contract, a version policy, and a support route.

gates.rule: the interface contract and its limits are written where consumers read them
consumers depend on a named version, not on a moving branch
at least one real consumer integrated and verified it
questions have a named first responder and a docs path

sections.title: Public contract
sections.purpose: What consumers may rely on, and what is explicitly not promised.

sections.title: Version and support policy
sections.purpose: How it changes, how long old versions live, and what counts as breaking.

sections.title: Packaging and distribution
sections.purpose: What ships, where it lands offline, and how integrity is checked.

sections.title: Adoption path
sections.purpose: The steps a consuming project takes, and how each is verified.

sections.title: Support and escalation
sections.purpose: Where a question goes first, and who is woken if it is on fire.

provide.catalog_template: Provide {subject} with capability detection, offline mocks, platform-specific implementations, error recovery, compatibility tests, and documented limitations for every supported target.
